verdict.rationale: MoQ Relay's own documented role is connecting live publishers to subscribers. A production report (SageOx) shows browser and device clients publishing Opus audio to one relay that fans out live to a transcription subscriber while sessions run. However, the transcription consumer is custom subscriber code, and the report notes real caveats: the first audio group was lost to a subscribe race, the transport falsely reported 'connected', and the relay does not preserve packet timing. missing for 10: a first-party connector or documented integration that streams to transcription/realtime model endpoints, first-party docs for an audio-to-AI pipeline, and reliable timing/start-of-stream guarantees without workarounds.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, live session audio can be streamed to a transcription or realtime model endpoint while the session is running

citations.quote: Browser, desktop, mobile and device clients publish Opus to one relay, which fans out to independent subscribers: an S3 archiver, Zoom Scribe Live transcription, and voice ID.
A server connecting publishers to subscribers, able to form a [self-hosted CDN cluster](/bin/relay/cluster.html).
the relay by design does not preserve packet identity or timing.
